names.official: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis

summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis waives visas for citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, most Commonwealth countries and much of Latin America — normally for up to 90 days — while CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. Every foreign visitor, visa-exempt or not, must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA, USD 17) online before travel. Nationals of the 67 countries and territories on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa-required list need a visa, applied for online through the Ministry of National Security's e-visa platform.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal for anyone, including children, to dress in camouflage clothing, with a fine of EC$250 and 3 months in prison; the Government of Canada adds that carrying items made of camouflage material is also illegal.
You must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty, according to the UK Foreign Office.

The UK Foreign Office says drug offences carry severe penalties: on conviction at a Magistrates Court, a fine of up to EC$400,000 or 3 times the street value, whichever is higher, and up to 10 years in prison; High Court sentences start at 15 years. Personal-use cannabis is decriminalised but needs a licence.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says US currency and major credit cards are accepted and ATMs are widely available. The UK Foreign Office notes that taxis are not metered and can often be paid in US dollars as well as EC dollars.

safety.text: Canada advises normal security precautions in Saint Kitts and Nevis. Petty crime such as pickpocketing and purse snatching occurs, as does violent crime including armed robbery and sexual assault; avoid isolated areas and unpatrolled beaches after dark, and keep car doors locked when driving.

tips.text: The hurricane season runs from June to November, according to the UK Foreign Office and the Government of Canada. Canada says even small tropical storms can quickly develop into major hurricanes during this period, and to weigh the risks carefully when planning a trip in that season.

Traffic drives on the left. The UK Foreign Office says you must have a St Kitts and Nevis driving licence: a temporary one is sold by the Inland Revenue Department, valid for 3 months (EC$62.50) or one year (EC$125), on showing your home licence and passport, and hire companies will usually help.
St Kitts and Nevis are separate islands; the Government of Canada says ferry services run between them and to Antigua and Barbuda and Montserrat.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Kitts and Nevis?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, most Commonwealth countries and much of Latin America are admitted visa-free for up to 90 days, and CARICOM nationals for six months. Nationals of the 67 countries and territories on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa-required list need a visa, applied for online through the Ministry of National Security's e-visa platform. Every foreign visitor, visa-exempt or not, must also obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA, USD 17) at knatravelform.kn before travel.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Kitts and Nevis without a visa?
faq.answer: Usually up to 90 days, with the officer writing the actual period on your entry stamp. It can be shorter if your return ticket is sooner. Extensions are handled by the Immigration Department in Basseterre and must be requested before the stamp expires.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Saint Kitts and Nevis?
faq.answer: Yes. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says citizens and visitors must complete the online Immigration and Customs (ED) form at knatravelform.kn. Fill it in before you travel, or on arrival on your own device.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens travel to Saint Kitts and Nevis visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes. Mainland China is not on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of the 67 countries and territories whose nationals need a visa, so Chinese citizens enter without one; the immigration officer sets the length of stay on arrival. Taiwanese (ROC) passport holders are also admitted visa-free, for up to 90 days. Either way, every foreign visitor must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA, USD 17) at knatravelform.kn before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Saint Kitts and Nevis?
faq.answer: No. The eTA platform run by the Ministry of National Security says there are currently no vaccination requirements to enter. WHO's list still shows a certificate requirement for arrivals from yellow fever risk countries, so if you are coming from one, carrying your certificate costs nothing.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply here?
faq.answer: Yes. As a CARICOM and OECS member, Saint Kitts and Nevis grants nationals of member states a definite entry of up to six months on arrival, without a visa. An Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) at knatravelform.kn is still required before travel; OECS nationals can apply with a national ID card.
